newsitem.title: USA: New York Times plans $20 mln ad campaign.
newsitem.headline: New York Times plans $20 mln ad campaign.

text.p: The New York Times Co said Tuesday it plans to spend $20 million on an advertising campaign to promote its image nationwide.
The campaign is aimed at reinforcing its image among loyal readers and a "like-minded" audience across the nation, the company said. Its theme is "Expect the World."

"As we expand nationally, this national image campaign is a major, long-range commitment to build our brand and ensure that The New York Times name remains synonymous with quality, intelligence and trustworthiness," Times President Janet Robinson said in a statement.

The campaign is to premiere February 2 with three, 30-second advertisements during Westinghouse Electric Corp's CBS-TV's "60 Minutes" program. The television ads are to appear throughout that week on other news magazine and analysis shows on CBS, General Electric Co's NBC and Walt Disney Co's ABC.
The media campaign is booked through June in national outlets, the company said. A simultaneous print campaign will run in The Times, as well as other publications.
